brief: Citi's Friday wire: risk stayed contained as Brent's rally to $117, highest since May on reports of US/Israeli strikes on Iran, pushed global yields higher, with the 10y UST retesting 5% and unwinding part of Thursday's 16bp CTA short-covering rally. Stronger October PMI and U. of Michigan data reaffirmed a stickier inflation backdrop. SPX fell 0.47% on lighter participation and weaker breadth, and vol stayed elevated, VVIX above 110, on anxiety ahead of next week's calendar: Fed, ECB, BoJ and BoC meetings all expected to hold, Warsh's guidance the Fed's key variable, RBNZ expected to hike 25bp, the UK Autumn Budget, US GDP, core PCE and ECI data, 41% of SPX market cap reporting (Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon), AI spending commentary in focus, $213bn of Treasury supply, and Brazilian (Sunday) and Israeli (Tuesday) elections. Datafolha shows Lula and Bolsonaro tied 50/50, tighter than the prior Quaest poll, and Citi positions for a Bolsonaro win. Gold slipped below $4,000 and the dollar firmed, pressuring EUR and GBP. TMT credit spreads widened on AI-spending angst and heavy issuance, flows skewed to hedge-fund downside protection. Citi's rates desk fades the richening, short the belly via a 5s7s10s fly ahead of next week's 7y auction.
